sections.label: PSP against CECA racism link
sections.summary: The Progress Singapore Party states it is categorically against linking public discourse on CECA to racism.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I hereby state categorically that the Progress Singapore Party (PSP) is against linking the public discourse on CECA to racism.

sections.label: CECA is trade agreement
sections.summary: The Singapore-India CECA is a trade agreement issue, not a race issue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Singapore-India CECA, is not a race issue but a trade agreement issue.

sections.label: Government CECA information unconvincing
sections.summary: Government disclosures are not convincing enough to prove CECA has not affected immigration management and has generated net benefits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: As of today, the information disclosed by the Government is not convincing enough to prove that CECA has not affected Singapore's ability to manage immigration and that it has generated net benefits for Singapore.

sections.label: 2008 PR angst high
sections.summary: Singaporean angst peaked in 2008 when 80,000 PRs were given to work pass holders that year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The angst among Singaporeans reached a high in 2008 when, in that year alone, 80,000 PRs were given out to work pass holders.

sections.label: Population growth before White Paper
sections.summary: By the January 2013 Population White Paper, population had grown 40% since the late 1990s.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: By the time the Population White Paper was released in January 2013, our population had already grown by 40% since the late 1990s.

sections.label: Pass holders and lower-wage workers
sections.summary: Singapore hosts pass holders and PRs in its PMET workforce, alongside lower-wage workers, gig workers and underemployed Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: On the one hand, Singapore is hosting 400,000, maybe 350,000 now, pass holders, and 250,000 Permanent Residents, accounting for about 20% and 15% of its PMET workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: On the other hand, Singapore has 500,000 lower-wage workers who need Government financial aid to live decently, and more than 100,000 gig workers deprived of basic employment benefits and future prospects, and hundreds of thousands of Singaporeans under the various job support schemes and many more underemployed, including the increasing number of self-employed workers.

sections.label: Doubts on net job creation
sections.summary: Singaporeans doubt net job creation for Singaporeans and want the Manpower Minister to clarify whether 380,000 PME jobs from 2005 to 2020 were net job creation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: However, many Singaporeans doubt whether there is net job creation for Singaporeans after stripping out the immigration effect from the employment statistics, the statistics which lump Singaporeans and PRs together in a category called "Residents".

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Hence, Singaporeans would like to clarify with the Manpower Minister whether the 380,000 PME jobs supposedly created for locals from 2005 to 2020 represent a net job creation for Singaporeans during that period.

sections.label: Underemployment and employer preferences
sections.summary: Singaporeans want the Manpower Minister to confirm whether employers prefer work pass holders, whether MOM monitors underemployment, and whether the objective is protecting jobs for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: For example, a Singaporean may want to work for eight hours a day, five days a week, but can only find enough work for four hours a day, two days a week.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: She is still considered employed, as a person is considered employed as long as she has worked for at least one hour during the reference period under our employment statistics.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: New graduates and the 40- to 50-year-old local PMETs are the most vulnerable to the underemployment trap because the former does not have work experience, and the latter needs to keep working to pay the bills.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Hence, Singaporeans would like to confirm with the Manpower Minister again, (a) whether there are not enough Singaporeans to meet employers' demand or employers prefer work pass holders; (b) is MOM monitoring underemployment; and (c) is the objective of the Government to protect jobs for Singaporeans or just to protect jobs?

sections.label: EP and S Pass salaries
sections.summary: Even with the late 2020 revision, EP and S Pass salaries are only $4,500 and $3,500, with much lower levels in earlier years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Even with the latest revision in late 2020, the respective salaries for EPs and S Passes are at $4,500 and $3,500 only, not to mention the much lower levels in the earlier years.

sections.label: EPs in senior finance positions
sections.summary: EPs occupy 57% of senior positions in the finance sector and 30% in domestic retail banking.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Yet, the EPs occupy 57% of the senior positions in the finance sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: And even in the domestic retail banking sub-sector, which serves essentially the local customers, they occupy 30% of the senior positions.

sections.label: EPs avoid employer CPF contribution
sections.summary: EPs enjoy an advantage over Singaporeans because their employers do not pay the 17% employer's CPF contribution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In addition to the low qualifying salary described above, the EPs enjoy an advantage over their Singaporean counterparts because their employers do not have to pay the 17% employer's CPF contribution.

sections.label: Fair Consideration Framework ineffectiveness
sections.summary: The Fair Consideration Framework is ineffective as labour market testing because work pass holders concentrated in certain sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The ineffectiveness of the Fair Consideration Framework as a form of labour market testing is obvious as the work pass holders were seen concentrating themselves in certain sectors.

sections.label: Work pass salary and nationality caps
sections.summary: Proposes raising EP and SP qualifying salaries, a $1,200 monthly EP levy, and a single-nationality cap aiming for 10%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: One, first and foremost, in order to raise the quality of our work pass holders, we should increase the qualifying salaries for EPs and SPs to $10,000 and $4,500 respectively in stages, over the next three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In addition, a standard monthly levy of $1,200 on all EPs should be introduced immediately to reduce unfair wage competition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Two, to break up concentration and to eradicate discrimination, we should impose a cap on workers from a single nationality, based on the percentage of a company's staff strength in each of its business function.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In the long term, we aim for a 10% single nationality cap to ensure diversity in our workforce and seek talent from different parts of the world instead of predominantly from one country or region.

sections.label: Reducing PRs and citizenships
sections.summary: Proposes reducing annual PRs and new citizenships for work pass holders in line with foreign manpower tightening to aid social integration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Three, the number of PRs and new citizenships awarded to work pass holders each year should be reduced to be in sync with the overall tightening of the foreign manpower to foster a longer period of social integration in order to reinvigorate our national identity.
